subtitle: Move from simply displaying an equity dashboard to using it for decisions. You will read its measures faithfully, compare possible next choices and review what changed with the people actually responsible.
scope: For staff and leaders across DHS. All people, routes, figures and encounters are original example. The first and later intervals each contain forty unique requests per invented processing route, counted once; the intervals do not follow the same people. The same event is a recorded help-finding explanation, not receipt, understanding, use or resolved need. Labels are not demographic groups or actual eligibility conditions. No intervention or cause is supplied. Separate follow-up-completion figures remain unknown. Community-display meanings and Sorrel’s allegation are separate illustrations. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Actual information and decision duties remain. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referral-only to the person or area responsible within ADSA.
introTranscript: Follow Petra and Dorian as they define a help-finding measure, distinguish known figures from missing information and compare useful next choices. Consider personally offered meanings in a separate encounter and retain actual information and reporting responsibilities. Read a later practice comparison without assuming a cause or wider result.

intro.heading: Begin with the question the dashboard serves
intro.body:
In an original practice DHS learning case, analyst Petra prepares a dashboard for a discussion with Dorian, who sponsors a proposed review of a help-finding process. One measure counts requests with a recorded explanation of where to seek help if an initial route does not work. During the first illustration interval, invented Route A has thirty of forty requests with that recorded explanation, 75 percent. Invented Route B has eighteen of forty, 45 percent. Each request is counted once within its route. The descriptive difference is thirty percentage points. These are invented processing labels, not demographic identities, actual service standards or DHS results.

Petra first titles the measure successful help. Dorian asks what was actually counted. The record concerns an explanation, not whether a person read it, could use it, obtained further help or had a need resolved. Changing the heading to recorded help-finding explanation makes the measure easier to interpret. It does not diminish the value of the question; it keeps a wider service outcome from being claimed through a narrower event.

Across both routes, forty-eight of eighty requests contain the event, 60 percent overall. That is useful for an overall question, while the route comparison makes the thirty-point difference visible. Neither figure explains its cause. The dashboard does not show why the explanation is absent from other requests or identify an individual’s effort, language, disability or cultural preference. A missing event during an interval is not proof that help was never available.

Dorian wants the display to support a practical inquiry: what evidence would help examine the difference and the experience of finding another help route? The measure can inform that question. A chart, heading and possible next question do not themselves establish authority to revise a service, allocate resources or publish actual information. A useful account should keep those distinctions visible rather than let a polished display appear to have made an official decision.

The GAO overview of data reliability emphasizes accuracy, completeness and applicability to the intended purpose. A dashboard is therefore more than its appearance. Its event definition, included requests, interval and limitations determine whether the figure fits the question. In actual work, a measure may support monitoring, exploration, a particular decision or another legitimate purpose. It need not meet a universal rule that every tile independently produces a decision by a fixed date before it has any value.

Privately describe the event, two levels, difference and one question the display cannot answer. You can use the full example without obtaining an actual record. Notice whether an attractive heading tempts you to assume a result the counts do not establish. A faithful dashboard can make an important question visible while leaving cause, responsible decisions and wider experience open.

accordion.heading: Examine the measure and its consequences

items.title: Give the event its actual name
items.body: Successful help would describe more than the supplied record. Petra’s revised heading identifies the recorded explanation. Readers can consider the help-finding question without assuming actual receipt, use or resolution. The revision repairs interpretation rather than proving that the underlying process improved.

items.title: Keep the relevant comparison visible
items.body: The overall 60 percent and two route levels answer connected but different questions. Dorian can show them together when examining the routes. A combined figure does not erase the difference, and a route gap does not establish a cause. The counts, bases and interval allow readers to understand the relationship.

items.title: Distinguish use from authority
items.body: A measure may be useful for monitoring or inquiry without producing an immediate operating decision. Actual choices retain appropriate roles, evidence and authority. Adding a name or target beside the tile cannot itself approve a change, establish resources or demonstrate that an outcome occurred.

tabs.label: The heading overstates the event
tabs.body: Petra labels the tile successful help. The records count a help-finding explanation, not resolved need. Dorian asks what the number means, and the heading is revised. A narrower accurate description retains a useful question while removing an unsupported outcome.

tabs.label: The combined figure replaces the question
tabs.body: The account shows only 48 of 80, 60 percent, while the meeting concerns route differences. Petra retains the overall figure and adds 75 and 45 percent with the 30-point gap. This restores the comparison without inventing its cause.

tabs.label: The purpose and limits are connected
tabs.body: The dashboard describes the recorded explanation and supports a question about the routes and actual experience. Dorian keeps operating decisions separate from the display. The proposal is useful without a completed policy change or a universal requirement that every tile produce immediate action.

check.question: What does the first practice comparison establish?
check.correct: Thirty of forty Route A requests and eighteen of forty Route B requests have the recorded explanation, 75 and 45 percent, a descriptive 30-percentage-point difference in one interval.
wrong: Everyone in Route A had their need resolved.
Route B users’ effort caused the difference.
A polished chart approves a service change.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The event, levels and difference stay at their supplied scale.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A recorded explanation does not establish resolved need. No causal or individual-effort evidence is supplied. Visual presentation does not create operating authority.

Route B has 18 recorded explanations among 40 requests.
Was the explanation understandable and usable?

Every person in Route A had a resolved need.
The chart authorizes a service revision.

lessons.title: Make missing information visible
lessons.summary: Read a blank or colored status according to its evidence rather than treat absence as zero or reassurance.
lessons.objective: Distinguish known event counts from missing information in the practice dashboard.
objectives: Distinguish known event counts from missing information in the practice dashboard.
Explain why a colored status does not establish success without its meaning and evidence.
Develop an accessible account that preserves essential values and relationships.
takeaways: Color can assist a display but should not carry its meaning alone.
A usable explanation preserves the question rather than merely repeat a chart title.
lessons.statement: Show what the measure means and distinguish unknown information from a recorded zero.

image.caption: Four people stand together; one holds papers and another holds a cup.

intro.heading: Make missing information visible
intro.body:
Petra adds a second display element labeled later follow-up completion. In the example, no figures have been supplied for that element. The dashboard originally shows a green circle beside it because there are no entries flagged as problems. Dorian initially interprets the circle as evidence that follow-up is complete. That conclusion is not supported. No completion data are supplied, and no basis for a favorable status is established. The absence of a warning is not evidence that an event occurred or an outcome improved.

The distinction between missing and zero is important. If a valid measure had a defined base and recorded zero events, that would be a particular finding. Here, neither a completion count nor a relevant base is supplied. Petra should describe the status as information not supplied rather than enter zero to make the dashboard appear complete. Filling the cell for visual symmetry would make the display less honest even if the page looked calmer.

The first measure does contain evidence: thirty of forty and eighteen of forty recorded help-finding explanations in one interval. Those figures can be described while the separate follow-up-completion element remains unknown. The whole dashboard need not disappear because one question lacks data. Equally, the known explanation counts cannot be used as substitute completion counts. A faithful display allows different measures to retain different evidence states.

Color introduces another reading question. W3C’s guidance on use of color explains why meaning needs another visual indication, such as text or shape, rather than color alone. A reader who cannot distinguish the hues should still be able to understand what a status means. In this case, an explicit information-not-supplied label is needed because the evidence is missing, not simply because the circle’s color is hard to see. Adding words can address that meaning problem without establishing that every feature of the dashboard is accessible.

Complex charts also need a fitting account of essential values and relationships beyond the image alone. Petra can explain the two counts, their bases, interval and thirty-point comparison in text or an appropriate structured presentation. Repeating chart of help does not communicate the actual finding. The guidance offers different approaches; it does not mean that one paragraph, table or automatic test certifies an entire dashboard or makes its content appropriate for every audience.

Privately contrast the known explanation finding with the unknown completion element. Write an understandable description of the comparison without using a color word as the result. No actual file, account or record is needed. The improvement is an accurate account of evidence and missing information. It is not proof that follow-up was completed or that a new display has already removed every access barrier.

accordion.heading: Examine the measure and its consequences

items.title: Keep the two measures separate
items.body: The recorded-explanation measure has supplied counts and bases. Later follow-up completion has neither. Petra can present the known comparison while labeling the second element unknown. Reusing the first measure’s figures for the second would confuse events rather than fill an evidence gap.

items.title: Do not convert absence into reassurance
items.body: No entries flagged as problems is not proof of completed follow-up. A green circle can make that mistaken inference easy. The status needs to reflect the actual evidence rather than the desire for a positive page. Missing information supports a question about what is needed, not a no-warning-signs conclusion.

items.title: Provide a meaningful account
items.body: The chart explanation retains 30 of 40 and 18 of 40, the common interval and 30-point gap. Text or another fitting account helps readers understand essential values and relationships. Words beside a color also need the correct meaning. These steps improve the specific account without certifying every accessibility requirement or authorizing disclosure.

tabs.label: A blank becomes a zero
tabs.body: Petra inserts zero completions into the second measure to avoid an empty cell. Neither its count nor base is supplied. Dorian asks that the absence stay visible as information not supplied. Zero would be an invented numerical finding, not a harmless display convention.

tabs.label: A circle supplies a reassuring story
tabs.body: Dorian reads green as completed follow-up because no problems are flagged. The record contains no completion evidence. Petra replaces the reassuring status with an explicit unknown label and leaves the next evidence question open. A new color is not the substance of the correction.

tabs.label: Different evidence states remain understandable
tabs.body: The first measure keeps its supplied route comparison; the separate completion element says information not supplied. Essential values and relationships have a fitting readable account beyond color alone. Readers can see what is known without treating one measure as proof of another.

check.question: How should the second completion element be described?
check.correct: As information not supplied, distinct from the known explanation counts, with no invented zero or favorable status.
wrong: As zero completions because the cell is blank.
As successful follow-up because the circle is green.
As 45 percent because that is the known Route B explanation level.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. This keeps the missing evidence and different event visible.
check.feedbackIncorrect: No count or base is supplied for a zero finding. A color and absence of flags do not establish completion. The explanation level cannot substitute for a different event’s unknown figures.

sorting.heading: Keep evidence, questions and conclusions distinct

items.text: Later completion figures are not supplied.
The explanation measure retains its own supplied counts.
Label a status with text rather than color alone.
Explain essential chart values and relationships in a fitting account.

responses: No completion evidence supports the favorable status.

lessons.transfer: Privately describe a known figure and an unknown measure without relying on color or inventing a zero.

lessons.title: Develop a useful choice through the actual roles
lessons.summary: Connect the finding to options, evidence and responsibility without allowing a dashboard to make the decision.
lessons.objective: Compare adding display detail with addressing the actual help-finding question.
objectives: Compare adding display detail with addressing the actual help-finding question.
Develop a reasoned recommendation that identifies needed evidence and responsible decisions.
Distinguish measure maintenance, operational authority and an agreed next inquiry.
takeaways: A useful next choice explains why it fits the question.
Maintaining the measure and deciding an operating change are different roles.
Naming responsibility does not itself supply approval or resources.
lessons.statement: Make the next choice understandable and locate who actually carries it.

image.caption: Four people stand together; one holds papers and another holds a cup.

intro.heading: Develop a useful choice through the actual roles
intro.body:
Petra and Dorian consider what to do with the first route comparison. One proposal is to add more charts using the same counts. Another is to prepare a clear finding and examine what evidence and perspectives could help understand the recorded-explanation difference. The second proposal responds more directly to their stated question. More display detail may be useful for another purpose, but repeating the same evidence in new shapes does not explain why the routes differ or show whether people can find help.

The comparison does not yet justify a particular operational fix. A proposal to require a new script assumes that wording caused the gap, even though the actual explanation materials are not supplied. A proposal to train Route B staff assumes a staff-performance cause the counts do not establish. These possibilities can be considered as questions, but their evidentiary basis and alternatives need examination before a recommendation treats either as the established remedy. Responsible analysis does not automatically prefer an individual or process cause because it sounds more plausible or fair.

Petra’s measure role is to explain the event, included requests, interval, calculation and known limitations. That role can include communicating uncertainty and checking whether the data fit the intended use. It does not make her powerless to contribute a reasoned proposal. Nor does it automatically authorize a staffing, service or spending decision. Actual authority depends on the task and assigned process, not a universal rule that an analyst can never own a particular inquiry or that a sponsor can decide every operational issue.

Dorian proposes considering a focused review of the event definition, relevant material and perspectives. The pair can describe the next question and identify which actual responsibilities would be needed for an inquiry. They can record the proposal’s status accurately: under consideration, not approved or performed. A name beside the tile is helpful when it explains the role, but it does not create resources, permission to collect information or authority to assign other people’s work.

An appropriate later review would ask what was actually agreed, what was done, what evidence became available and what remains open. Its timing and setting should fit the work and responsible decisions. This course creates no universal quarterly meeting, Friday deadline, three-to-five-tile limit or required public log. The important principle is traceable follow-through at the actual scale, including an honest account when a proposal has not been approved or a result has not been observed.

Privately compare the two initial proposals and write a reason for the focused inquiry. Then identify a task the measure can support and an operating decision it cannot authorize. You may use the example without creating a live project or assigning colleagues. A recommendation can be useful before it specifies a remedy, when it explains the question, needed evidence and responsibilities well enough for actual consideration.

accordion.heading: Examine the measure and its consequences

items.title: Compare the purpose of the options
items.body: More charts can add useful detail in some situations. Here the central question concerns the difference in the event and experience of finding help. A focused evidence inquiry serves that purpose more directly than new shapes made from the same counts. This does not establish one universal maximum number of tiles.

items.title: Do not prescribe a cause through a remedy
items.body: A required script or staff training might seem like a clear next action. The counts do not show whether wording or staff performance caused the difference. Petra can identify those as possible questions and examine appropriate evidence rather than let the proposed remedy silently certify its own explanation.

items.title: Give responsibility its actual basis
items.body: The measure role and operating authority can be described without reducing the analyst to a powerless maintainer or making the sponsor an all-purpose decision maker. Actual assignment, evidence and process matter. A proposed inquiry and named role are useful context, not approved collection, resources or completed action.

tabs.label: New tiles substitute for the question
tabs.body: The pair adds several shapes containing the same 30 of 40 and 18 of 40 counts. The display becomes larger while the cause and experience questions stay unanswered. Dorian can consider whether added detail genuinely serves a purpose or whether the focused inquiry is a better next proposal.

tabs.label: A proposed fix supplies its own cause
tabs.body: Petra recommends compulsory Route B training as if the counts proved staff performance was the cause. The records do not establish that. A more reasoned proposal distinguishes possible explanations, needed evidence and actual roles before choosing a remedy.

tabs.label: A justified inquiry retains honest status
tabs.body: The pair proposes reviewing the event definition, relevant material and perspectives because important questions remain open. They identify responsibilities needed to consider an actual method. No approval, information collection or service change is supplied. The recommendation is useful because its reason and limits are understandable.

check.question: Which recommendation follows the supplied evidence?
check.correct: Propose a focused inquiry into the event definition, fitting evidence and relevant experience, identifying actual responsibilities and keeping remedies and approval open.
wrong: Require Route B training because the counts prove poor staff performance.
Approve a new service procedure because the sponsor’s name appears beside the tile.
Add charts and report that this explains the cause.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The proposal connects to the question without inventing a cause or decision.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The counts supply no staff-performance cause. A displayed name does not supply actual operating authority or an approved procedure. Repeating counts in new shapes does not establish why the difference occurred.

intro.heading: Learn what makes a result meaningful here
intro.body:
In a separate original voluntary community-display encounter, organizer Elva asks contributors what they want a display of shared work to show. Qarin asks whether one unfinished piece can be understood and used. Maia asks how contributions fit a wider sequence. Elva initially interprets Qarin as preoccupied with a tiny detail and Maia as avoiding a concrete result. No final display, exact contribution wording or permission to use their accounts is supplied.

Qarin offers a personally learned meaning from a quilting circle he chose to join. Before pieces became a larger design, making one connection fit allowed a contribution to become useful to someone else. A small result could have value before the whole pattern was complete. Maia offers a personally learned meaning from an orchard-observation circle she chose to join. Seeing how a change fit the season helped her understand what an isolated observation could and could not mean. The sequence made a particular result more intelligible rather than replacing the result with an abstract aspiration.

These accounts widen Elva’s first judgments. Qarin’s detailed question can express care for a usable contribution. Maia’s wider-pattern question can express care for context and interpretation. Both remain particular meanings from chosen experiences. They do not prove that everyone in those circles thinks alike, determine the speakers’ cultural identities or establish a preferred learning style or IDI position. Learning the meaning changes the inquiry without classifying a person.

Elva can revise the invitation to ask what usable contribution, meaningful connection or other result the person wants considered, and what context they choose to retain. A participant may use an example, offer a question or keep an experience private. No biography or agreement with a single value definition is required. Describing the invitation more carefully does not establish final wording, permission to display an account or a later improvement in trust. Those choices remain with the actual participants and process.

The encounter can inform Petra and Dorian’s habit of asking whether a dashboard question captures what matters. It cannot establish the cause of their route comparison or substitute a story for a recorded count. An actual affected perspective may help examine what a measure leaves out and which inquiry is useful. It should not be treated as representation of an entire community, proof of every result or a requirement that someone disclose enough personal history to justify attention.

Privately connect one initial label, one offered meaning and one change to the invitation. You can reflect unrecorded on why a small usable result or a wider connection matters to you without preparing an actual dashboard. A richer understanding is a legitimate learning result. It can support better questions while numerical evidence, actual permission and operational decisions continue to need their own basis.

items.title: Let the meanings widen interpretation
items.body: Qarin describes the value of a usable connection, while Maia describes the value of a sequence that helps interpretation. Elva can see more than preoccupation or avoidance. The response changes because the meanings are received, not because a particular circle is assigned a universal personality.

items.title: Keep choice in the invitation
items.body: The revised invitation makes room for a useful contribution, connection or another result. It does not require biography, fixed affiliation or public reflection. A person can choose an example or privacy. The invitation can be more fitting before display wording and actual use permission are decided.

items.title: Do not merge different kinds of evidence
items.body: The encounter develops a habit of asking what matters. It supplies no facts about the request routes or their causes. Relevant perspectives may help examine a measure’s purpose, but neither a story nor a chart automatically answers every question. Their actual scope should remain visible.

tabs.label: A particular meaning becomes a fixed group style
tabs.body: Elva assigns all quilting-circle participants a detail style and all orchard-circle participants a vague style. The example gives two chosen experiences and meanings, not a census or personality test. The label would close the inquiry that the accounts are meant to widen.

tabs.label: A story supplies an unrelated cause
tabs.body: Elva says the offered meanings explain Route B’s lower event rate. No connection between these contributors and the request records is supplied. The encounter can improve inquiry without becoming causal evidence about another illustration.

tabs.label: The invitation changes with the meanings
tabs.body: Elva asks what useful contribution, connection or other result matters here and what context the person chooses to retain. The proposed invitation responds to the actual meanings, while wording, agreement and display permission remain open. Neither numerical evidence nor personal choice is replaced.

intro.heading: Retain actual information and reporting responsibilities
intro.body:
Dorian wants to understand the unknown follow-up-completion element. He suggests linking the request list to personal records and adding filters to find possible explanations. Petra sees the value of the question, but the exercise supplies no actual records or permission for those uses. The choice to build a dashboard does not itself authorize new collection, linkage, access or disclosure. A useful analysis can identify a question that needs an appropriate method rather than pretend that more information is available for unrestricted use.

Actual data responsibilities depend on purpose, classification, assignment and applicable arrangements. Minnesota Statutes section 13.05 addresses necessary collection and storage, purpose limitations, accuracy and safeguards for individual data. Its protections are not replaced by saying the dashboard is internal. Names removed from a view do not automatically guarantee anonymity, and small combined counts do not automatically establish safe disclosure. This lesson creates no universal minimum-count rule, retention period or authorization to collect new demographic fields.

An actual reporting or operating decision also needs its relevant authority. The dashboard’s proposed question does not approve service eligibility, contracts, expenditures, site visits or personnel decisions. Nor does every numerical difference automatically establish a particular complaint or legal trigger. Petra and Dorian can keep their inquiry useful while locating the actual responsibilities that apply. They should not invent a universal office, same-day referral schedule or one approval that supposedly covers all possible work.

A separate original learning example concerns supervisor Sorrel, who receives a religion-related harassment allegation while discussing dashboard presentation. Under MMB Policy 1436, managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow applicable agency procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. Sorrel does not wait for a chart to prove the allegation, a completed review, consensus, apology, course completion or consultant feedback. Assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain part of the actual process. Reporting the allegation is distinct from determining that a violation occurred.

Daily equity considerations and qualifying formal analyses retain their actual DHS tools and responsibilities. Actions with prolonged or long-term impact scheduled for specified leadership approval keep the formal analysis or scan, or a relevant customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director, described by the DHS Equity Policy. The dashboard may support that work, but the learning comparison does not automatically complete it. Staff carry their own equity work while the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback. Consultation is not a universal gate before using a resource or meeting an immediate duty.

Privately distinguish a useful question, an information use that needs appropriate consideration and an actual duty that continues. Use the example without obtaining a real record or entering an allegation. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referral-only to the person or area responsible within ADSA; no office contact is invented. The purpose is responsible inquiry with actual roles intact, rather than treating a data gap as permission or waiting for a dashboard meeting before carrying an obligation.

intro.heading: Review later evidence without turning a change into proof
intro.body:
The final lesson supplies a later practice comparison, separate from the first interval’s requests. Each route again contains forty unique requests counted once in its interval, and the same defined event is used: a recorded explanation of where to seek help when an initial route does not work. Route A now has thirty-two of forty, 80 percent. Route B has twenty-eight of forty, 70 percent. The later descriptive gap is ten percentage points. The two intervals do not follow the same people, and no intervention, operating approval or cause for the movement is supplied.

Compared with the first illustration interval, Route A’s recorded-event rate rises from 75 to 80 percent, five percentage points. Route B’s rises from 45 to 70 percent, twenty-five points. The gap narrows from thirty to ten points, a reduction of twenty points. Overall, sixty of eighty later requests have the event, 75 percent, compared with forty-eight of eighty, 60 percent earlier: an increase of fifteen points. These are changes in the defined practice measure, not percentages of individuals whose experience improved.

Petra can report the movement accurately. She cannot attribute it to the focused inquiry they proposed, because the example supplies no performed inquiry or intervention. Nor can she infer that an actual service policy, staff behavior, request mix or recording practice caused the rates to change. Those are possible lines of examination, not established explanations. The shared event definition helps compare the illustration, but it does not certify the reliability or comparability of every actual system that might produce a similar dashboard.

Dorian also keeps the wider experience visible. A recorded explanation still does not establish receipt, understanding, use or resolved need. The separate later-follow-up-completion element still has no supplied figures. Improved explanation rates do not fill that blank. A dashboard can show a favorable movement in one measure while another question remains unknown. Calling the whole process successful would collapse those different evidence states.

The pair’s closing recommendation describes the two intervals and proposes appropriate inquiry into what could explain the movement and whether the explanation is usable. The proposal remains under consideration. An actual review would need fitting evidence, perspectives, purpose, information arrangements and responsible decisions. Its timing should fit the work; the course does not impose a quarterly cycle or public log. Elva’s separate meaning encounter informs thoughtful inquiry, while Sorrel’s separate allegation preserves actual duties. Neither becomes part of the numerical comparison.

Privately write one supported change, one open explanation and one wider result that remains unknown. You can value the clearer account without an actual dashboard or public artifact. Staff carry their equity work with consultant program leadership, knowledge and feedback. The course’s result is a more faithful reading and next question, not proof that real services or staff development have improved.

items.title: Calculate each comparison explicitly
items.body: The later levels are 32 of 40, 80 percent, and 28 of 40, 70 percent. The gap is 10 points versus 30 earlier. Route changes are 5 and 25 points; overall 60 of 80 is 75 percent versus 60 percent earlier, a 15-point increase. Distinguishing levels and differences prevents a vague improved-by-twenty-percent claim.

items.title: Do not give the proposal credit for the movement
items.body: No actual inquiry or intervention is supplied. The recommendation cannot be said to have caused the later rates. Petra can report movement and identify evidence needed to examine explanations. That is more informative than refusing all comparison or declaring a favorite cause verified.

items.title: Keep the unknown element unknown
items.body: The separate completion element still has no figures. A favorable explanation-rate change is not a substitute for completion, understanding or resolved need. Dorian can acknowledge movement and maintain the open question. Missing wider evidence is neither automatic success nor no warning signs.

tabs.label: Movement becomes a causal success claim
tabs.body: Petra credits the proposed inquiry with narrowing the gap. No performed inquiry or intervention is supplied. Dorian separates the observed practice movement from its unknown cause. The change remains worth examining without an invented policy or training result.

tabs.label: One improved measure fills every blank
tabs.body: Dorian marks follow-up completion successful because explanation rates rose. Those events are distinct, and completion figures remain absent. Petra keeps the unknown label beside the supported later comparison. This preserves both the movement and the unanswered question.

tabs.label: The review supports the next inquiry
tabs.body: The account reports the later levels, route changes, narrowed gap and overall change. It keeps cause, actual proposal decisions and wider experience open. An appropriate next inquiry could examine those questions through actual responsibilities. The clearer account is useful without a guaranteed operational result.

sections.heading: Define the event and first comparison
items: Petra and Dorian’s example counts a recorded explanation of where to seek help if an initial route does not work. It does not establish receipt, understanding, use or resolved need.

In the first illustration interval, thirty of forty Route A requests and eighteen of forty Route B requests contain the event: 75 and 45 percent, a descriptive thirty-percentage-point difference. Each request is unique and counted once within the route.
Forty-eight of eighty requests have the event overall, 60 percent. The combined level and route comparison answer connected but different questions. Keep the relevant relationship visible.

The route labels are invented processing categories, not demographic groups, actual eligibility conditions or DHS results. The comparison supplies no cause, individual effort or later service outcome.

sections.heading: Show unknown information honestly and make the account usable
items: The separate later-follow-up-completion element has no supplied figures or base. Describe information not supplied rather than invent a zero, favorable status or completion percentage.
The known explanation counts cannot substitute for unknown completion. Different measures retain their different events and evidence states.
Color can assist presentation but should not be the only visual way to communicate information. A status also needs an honest meaning; a green circle cannot establish completion.

Give essential chart values and relationships a fitting readable account beyond the image alone. Repeating a title is not the same as describing the finding. These communication considerations do not certify the entire dashboard or authorize an actual public release.

sections.heading: Compare next choices and locate actual responsibility
items: New shapes made from the same counts do not explain the gap. A focused inquiry into the event definition, relevant material and experience fits the stated help-finding question more directly. Extra display detail may still serve another legitimate purpose.

A required script assumes a wording cause; Route B staff training assumes a performance cause. Neither is established. Keep possibilities as questions and identify evidence that could distinguish explanations before prescribing a remedy.

Measure maintenance includes a faithful definition, calculation and limits. Actual operating authority depends on assignment and process; an analyst is not automatically powerless, and a sponsor name does not authorize every change.

The proposed inquiry remains under consideration, not approved or performed. Describe appropriate responsibilities and needed evidence without inventing resources, collection permission, a universal quarterly meeting, public log or three-to-five-tile rule.

sections.heading: Learn what a result means to the person
items: In a separate voluntary community-display encounter, Qarin’s chosen quilting-circle meaning concerns a usable connection before the whole design is finished. Maia’s chosen orchard-observation meaning concerns a sequence that makes an observation intelligible.
Elva’s detail-preoccupation and result-avoidance labels widen. Ask what useful contribution, meaningful connection or other result matters here and what context the person chooses to retain.
Fiction or privacy remains available; no biography, fixed learning style, group trait or IDI position is established. Final wording, agreement, display permission and later trust remain open.
The meanings improve a habit of inquiry. They do not explain the request-route gap or replace numerical evidence. A relevant perspective can matter without representing a whole community.

sections.heading: Retain actual information and reporting duties
items: A dashboard question does not authorize unrestricted personal-record linkage, new fields, access or release. Internal viewing, removed names and combined counts are not automatic privacy guarantees. Actual purpose, classification, access and safeguards remain.

Minnesota Statutes section 13.05 addresses necessary collection and storage, purpose limitations, accuracy and safeguards. This course supplies no universal retention period, minimum-count rule or complete classification determination.

In the separate supervisor example, Sorrel immediately reports all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or agency AAO and follows applicable agency procedures or the Affirmative Action Plan. Proof, a meeting, apology, course or consultant feedback is not a condition. Assigned investigation and nonretaliation remain.

Daily equity considerations and qualifying formal analyses retain actual DHS tools and responsible roles. The chart does not approve services, eligibility, contracts, staffing, spending or personnel decisions. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters remain referred to the person or area responsible within ADSA, without an invented contact.

sections.heading: Review the later figures and keep results distinct
items: The later illustration uses forty new unique requests per route and the same defined event. Thirty-two of forty in Route A is 80 percent; twenty-eight of forty in Route B is 70 percent. The later gap is ten points. The intervals do not follow the same people.

Route A rises five percentage points from 75 to 80; Route B rises twenty-five from 45 to 70. The gap narrows twenty points from thirty to ten. Overall sixty of eighty is 75 percent versus 60 earlier, an increase of fifteen points.

No performed inquiry, intervention or cause is supplied. Movement cannot be attributed to the proposal. Wider receipt, understanding, use and resolved need remain unknown, as do the separate completion figures. A favorable explanation rate cannot fill that blank.

Return the supported change, open explanation, actual proposal status and fitting next question. Keep the numerical comparison, meaning encounter and allegation example separate. Staff carry work with consultant program leadership, knowledge and feedback; optional consultation is not a universal gate.
Private learning is meaningful without a live dashboard or public artifact. The clearer reading and proposal are progress without a claim of improved actual services.
